claim: Multiciliated cells (MCC) contain hundreds of motile cilia used to propel fluid over their surface.
source: Multiciliated cells (MCC) contain hundreds of motile cilia used to propel fluid over their surface.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the abstract describing the basic structure and function of multiciliated cells.

claim: Each MCC produces between 100-600 centrioles by a process termed centriole amplification.
source: To template these cilia, each MCC produces between 100-600 centrioles by a process termed centriole amplification.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a known characteristic of MCC.

claim: Airway progenitor cells contain two parental centrioles (PC) and form structures called deuterosomes that nucleate centrioles during amplification.
source: Airway progenitor cells contain two parental centrioles (PC) and form structures called deuterosomes that nucleate centrioles during amplification.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the abstract describing the cellular structures involved in centriole amplification.

claim: Ablation of PC does not perturb deuterosome formation and centriole amplification.
source: Using an ex vivo airway culture model, we show that ablation of PC does not perturb deuterosome formation and centriole amplification.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: Loss of PC caused an increase in deuterosome and centriole abundance.
source: In contrast, loss of PC caused an increase in deuterosome and centriole abundance, highlighting the presence of a compensatory mechanism.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by quantitative data in Figures 3 and 4.

claim: There is a linear relationship between surface area and centriole number in multiciliated cells.
source: Quantification of centriole abundance in vitro and in vivo identified a linear relationship between surface area and centriole number.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by quantitative data in Figures 4, 6, and 7.

claim: Centriole number scales with surface area.
source: By manipulating cell size, we discovered that centriole number scales with surface area.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental manipulation data in Figure 7.

claim: A cell-intrinsic surface area-dependent mechanism controls centriole and cilia abundance in multiciliated cells.
source: Our results demonstrate that a cell-intrinsic surface area-dependent mechanism controls centriole and cilia abundance in multiciliated cells.
evidence: This is the main conclusion stated in the abstract, based on the experimental findings.

claim: Multiciliated cells line the respiratory tract, brain ventricles and segments of the female and male reproductive organs in mammals.
source: In mammals, multiciliated cells (MCC) are terminally differentiated epithelia that line the respiratory tract, brain ventricles and segments of the female and male reproductive organs (Brooks and Wallingford, 2014; Spassky and Meunier, 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Motile cilia of MCC beat directionally to propel mucus and inhaled contaminants out of the lungs in the airway.
source: In the airway, motile cilia of MCC beat directionally to propel mucus and inhaled contaminants out of the lungs.
evidence: This is a statement of established biological function.

claim: Ciliary motility of ependymal MCC lining the brain ventricles is key for movement of cerebrospinal fluid through the central nervous system.
source: Ciliary motility of ependymal MCC lining the brain ventricles is key for movement of cerebrospinal fluid through the central nervous system, while cilia on MCC in the reproductive tracts are important for ovum and sperm transport (Brooks and Wallingford, 2014; Spassky and Meunier, 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Cilia on MCC in the reproductive tracts are important for ovum and sperm transport.
source: Ciliary motility of ependymal MCC lining the brain ventricles is key for movement of cerebrospinal fluid through the central nervous system, while cilia on MCC in the reproductive tracts are important for ovum and sperm transport (Brooks and Wallingford, 2014; Spassky and Meunier, 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Mutations that result in reduced cilia abundance cause human diseases due to aberrant cilia-based fluid flow.
source: Mutations that result in reduced cilia abundance cause human diseases due to aberrant cilia-based fluid flow (Amirav et al., 2016; Boon et al., 2014; Núnez-Ollé et al., 2017; Wallmeier et al., 2014), suggesting that establishment of the correct number of cilia per cell is important for function.
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to previous literature.

claim: MCC in different tissues display significant variability in motile cilia number, ranging from 30 to 600 cilia per cell.
source: MCC in different tissues display significant variability in motile cilia number, ranging from 30 to 600 cilia per cell (Brooks and Wallingford, 2014; Spassky and Meunier, 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Proliferating airway progenitors (basal cells) initially contain a single centrosome with two parental centrioles.
source: In the airway, proliferating progenitors (called basal cells) initially contain a single centrosome with two parental centrioles (PC), which they maintain via the canonical centriole duplication mechanism (Figure 1a; Nigg and Holland, 2018; Sorokin, 1968; Vladar and Stearns, 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature and referenced to Figure 1a.

claim: Post-mitotic basal cells undergo massive centriole production through two parallel pathways: a parental centriole-dependent pathway and an acentriolar or 'de novo' pathway mediated by deuterosomes.
source: During MCC differentiation, the post-mitotic basal cells undergo massive centriole production that was thought to occur through two parallel pathways: a parental centriole-dependent pathway whereby the original PC template the assembly of multiple procentrioles simultaneously, and an acentriolar or 'de novo' pathway mediated by dozens of deuterosomes, spheroidal electron-dense structures that are capable of producing multiple procentrioles (Figure 1a; Kalnins and Porter, 1969; Sorokin, 1968; Steinman, 1968).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature and referenced to Figure 1a.

claim: Deuterosomes are transient structures that are absent in proliferating progenitor cells, are formed during early centriole amplification, and mostly disappear after centriologenesis is complete.
source: Deuterosomes are transient structures that are absent in proliferating progenitor cells, are formed during early centriole amplification, and mostly disappear after centriologenesis is complete (Klos Dehring et al., 2013; Zhao et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The deuterosome-dependent pathway contributes the majority (80–90%) of the total centrioles assembled during amplification.
source: It has been estimated that the deuterosome-dependent pathway contributes the majority (80–90%) of the total centrioles assembled during amplification, while the PC-dependent pathway contributes roughly 10–20% towards the final number (Al Jord et al., 2014; Sorokin, 1968; Spassky and Meunier, 2017; Zhao et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The PC-dependent pathway contributes roughly 10–20% towards the final centriole number.
source: It has been estimated that the deuterosome-dependent pathway contributes the majority (80–90%) of the total centrioles assembled during amplification, while the PC-dependent pathway contributes roughly 10–20% towards the final number (Al Jord et al., 2014; Sorokin, 1968; Spassky and Meunier, 2017; Zhao et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Deuterosomes themselves are nucleated from the original PC.
source: Intriguingly, a recent study found that deuterosomes themselves are nucleated from the original PC, indicating that these two pathways may not be independent of each other after all (Al Jord et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Control cells at ALI0 predominantly contain the original two PC.
source: Control cells at ALI0 predominantly contain the original two PC (Figure 1b–c).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1b-c.

claim: Growth of basal cells in the presence of 1 µM Centrinone resulted in >80% of cells lacking PC at ALI0.
source: Growth of basal cells in the presence of 1 µM Centrinone resulted in >80% of cells lacking PC at ALI0 (Figure 1b–c).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1b-c.

claim: The formation of centriolar aggregates and subsequent centriole amplification proceeded normally in the absence of PC.
source: Remarkably, the formation of centriolar aggregates and subsequent centriole amplification proceeded normally in the absence of PC.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by data in Figures 1 and 2.

claim: There was no significant difference in the timing of centriologenesis, or the fraction of MCC in the population upon Centrinone treatment.
source: Moreover, there was no significant difference in the timing of centriologenesis, or the fraction of MCC in the population (Figure 1b–c).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1b-c.

claim: There was >80% decrease in cells containing PC upon Centrinone treatment as confirmed by TEM.
source: Whereas PC were evident in control cells, there was >80% decrease in cells containing PC upon Centrinone treatment (Figure 1d and Figure 1—video 1), consistent with the immunofluorescence analysis.
evidence: This is supported by TEM data shown in Figure 1d.

claim: Centrinone-mediated inhibition of Plk4 kinase activity blocks autophosphorylation-induced degradation, resulting in elevated (yet inactive) Plk4 protein levels.
source: Centrinone-mediated inhibition of Plk4 kinase activity blocks this degradation, resulting in elevated (yet inactive) Plk4 protein levels (Wong et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: In control cells, Plk4 expression increased during early stages of centriole amplification, peaking at ALI3 and subsequently decreasing upon centriole maturation at ALI8.
source: In control cells, Plk4 expression increased during early stages of centriole amplification, peaking at ALI3 and subsequently decreasing upon centriole maturation at ALI8 (Figure 2a–b).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2a-b.

claim: Centrinone-treated cells showed accumulation of Plk4, which was already evident in a higher proportion of cells at ALI0-1.
source: Centrinone-treated cells showed accumulation of Plk4, which was already evident in a higher proportion of cells at ALI0-1 (Figure 2a).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2a.

claim: The high Plk4-expressing fraction persisted at ALI8 and beyond in Centrinone-treated cells, indicating that Plk4 kinase activity was indeed blocked.
source: Unlike control cells, the high Plk4-expressing fraction persisted at ALI8 and beyond (Figure 2a–b), indicating that Plk4 kinase activity was indeed blocked.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2a-b and represents an inference from the data.

claim: Loss of PC did not affect the overall timing of centriole amplification stages, or the fraction of MCC in the population.
source: Loss of PC did not affect the overall timing of centriole amplification stages, or the fraction of MCC in the population (Figure 2c–g and Figure 2—figure supplements 1–2).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2c-g and supplementary figures.

claim: Centriole maturation and ciliogenesis were unaffected upon loss of PC and Plk4-inhibition.
source: Centriole maturation and ciliogenesis were also unaffected upon loss of PC and Plk4-inhibition (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: Parental centrioles and Plk4 kinase activity are not necessary for centriole amplification and ciliogenesis in airway MCC.
source: Collectively, these results indicate that parental centrioles and Plk4 kinase activity are not necessary for centriole amplification and ciliogenesis in airway MCC.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in Figures 1 and 2.

claim: Deup1 expression was grossly unchanged in cells lacking PC.
source: Surprisingly, Deup1 expression was grossly unchanged in cells lacking PC (Figure 3a–b).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3a-b.

claim: Deup1 foci were evident in a higher proportion of cells at ALI1, suggesting that deuterosome formation may start sooner in PC-less cells.
source: However, Deup1 foci were evident in a higher proportion of cells at ALI1, suggesting that deuterosome formation may start sooner in PC-less cells.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation of Deup1 expression patterns.

claim: Centrinone-treated cells lacking PC displayed a slight but significant increase in average deuterosome number per cell.
source: Centrinone-treated cells lacking PC displayed a slight but significant increase in average deuterosome number per cell (Figure 3d).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 3d.

claim: Serial-section TEM analysis of cells at ALI3 confirmed the presence of deuterosome structures that were nucleating procentrioles in PC-less cells.
source: Serial-section TEM analysis of cells at ALI3 confirmed the presence of deuterosome structures that were nucleating procentrioles in PC-less cells (Figure 3e).
evidence: This is supported by TEM data shown in Figure 3e.

claim: Deuterosomes in PC-less cells appeared consistent in size and morphology with control cells.
source: These deuterosomes appeared consistent in size and morphology with control cells.
evidence: This is an observation from TEM analysis.

claim: Deuterosomes in PC-less cells nucleated roughly similar amounts of procentrioles each as compared to control cells, with a slight decrease in average procentriole number per deuterosome.
source: Moreover, deuterosomes in PC-less cells nucleated roughly similar amounts of procentrioles each as compared to control cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 1), with a slight decrease in average procentriole number per deuterosome.
evidence: This is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Quantification of centriole number in control cells at ALI12 showed a range from 100 to 600, and correlated with increasing surface area.
source: Quantification of centriole number in control cells at ALI12 showed a range from 100 to 600, and correlated with increasing surface area (Figure 4a–b).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 4a-b.

claim: Loss of PC in Centrinone-treated cells did not disrupt the relationship between centriole number and surface area.
source: Loss of PC in Centrinone-treated cells did not disrupt this relationship (Figure 4c).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4c.

claim: The average number of centrioles per mature MCC did not decrease upon loss of PC; in contrast there was a slight but significant increase in centriole abundance and density.
source: Importantly, the average number of centrioles per mature MCC did not decrease; in contrast we noted a slight but significant increase in centriole abundance and density (Figure 4d–e).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 4d-e.

claim: Loss of PC does not inhibit deuterosome biogenesis nor result in decreased centriole abundance in MCC.
source: All together, these results indicate that loss of PC does not inhibit deuterosome biogenesis nor result in decreased centriole abundance in MCC.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in Figures 3 and 4.

claim: Plk4 expression becomes elevated during centriole amplification in airway MCC.
source: Plk4 expression becomes elevated during centriole amplification in airway MCC (Hoh et al., 2012), where it localizes to both PC and deuterosomes (Zhao et al., 2013), thus it has been generally assumed to play an important role in centriole amplification.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Plk4 localizes to both PC and deuterosomes.
source: Plk4 expression becomes elevated during centriole amplification in airway MCC (Hoh et al., 2012), where it localizes to both PC and deuterosomes (Zhao et al., 2013), thus it has been generally assumed to play an important role in centriole amplification.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Although Plk4 kinase activity is necessary for centriole duplication during the proliferation phase of basal cells, it is not essential for post-mitotic centriole amplification.
source: However, our Centrinone treatments suggest that although Plk4 kinase activity is necessary for centriole duplication during the proliferation phase of basal cells, it is not essential for post-mitotic centriole amplification (Figures 1–3).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in Figures 1-3.

claim: Depletion of Plk4 during the proliferation phase resulted in near complete loss of PC by ALI0.
source: Depletion of Plk4 during the proliferation phase resulted in near complete loss of PC by ALI0 (Figure 5a–b), similar to the Centrinone experiments.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 5a-b.

claim: Cells lacking Plk4 still initiate centriologenesis similar to control cells at ALI3.
source: Examination of cells at ALI3 showed that cells lacking Plk4 still initiate centriologenesis similar to control cells (Figure 5a,c and d), and form more deuterosomes on average (Figure 5a and e), consistent with the Centrinone-mediated experiments.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 5a, c, d, and e.

claim: Cells lacking Plk4 form more deuterosomes on average.
source: Examination of cells at ALI3 showed that cells lacking Plk4 still initiate centriologenesis similar to control cells (Figure 5a,c and d), and form more deuterosomes on average (Figure 5a and e), consistent with the Centrinone-mediated experiments.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 5a and e.

claim: Quantification of the fraction of MCC at ALI12 showed no overall difference between control and Plk4-depleted cells.
source: Moreover, quantification of the fraction of MCC at ALI12 showed no overall difference between control and Plk4-depleted cells.
evidence: This is supported by quantitative data in Figure 5.

claim: The process of centriole amplification appeared delayed in Plk4-depleted cells, as roughly 50% of Plk4-depleted cells at ALI12 were in Stages I-II or III-IV instead of being fully mature MCC.
source: However, the process of centriole amplification appeared delayed, as roughly 50% of Plk4-depleted cells at ALI12 were in Stages I-II or III-IV instead of being fully mature MCC (Figure 5a and f).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 5a and f.

claim: Culturing Plk4-depleted cells for an additional 9 days caused an increase in the fraction of mature MCC.
source: Indeed, culturing these Plk4-depleted cells for an additional 9 days caused an increase in the fraction of mature MCC (Figure 5a and g).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 5a and g.

claim: Once cells completed maturation, there was no significant decrease in centriole number per cell in Plk4-depleted cells.
source: Importantly, once cells completed maturation we did not observe a significant decrease in centriole number per cell (Figure 5h).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 5h.

claim: The dynamics of centriole biogenesis using a combination of shRNA-mediated depletion and Centrinone-based inhibition of Plk4 were almost identical to shRNA-mediated depletion alone, with no additive effects.
source: We found that the dynamics of centriole biogenesis were almost identical to shRNA-mediated depletion (Figure 5—figure supplement 1), with no additive effects.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Loss of Plk4 delays the centriole assembly program but does not decrease centriole abundance.
source: Collectively, these results indicate that loss of Plk4 delays the centriole assembly program but does not decrease centriole abundance.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in Figure 5.

claim: Constitutive expression of mChPlk4 during the proliferation stage resulted in cells that contained more than the normal complement of two PC at ALI0.
source: Constitutive expression of mChPlk4 during the proliferation stage resulted in cells that contained more than the normal complement of two PC at ALI0 (Figure 5i).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 5i.

claim: Mature MCC containing excess PC and Plk4 protein formed a similar number of centrioles when compared to control cells at ALI12.
source: However, mature MCC containing excess PC and Plk4 protein formed a similar number of centrioles when compared to control cells at ALI12 (Figure 5i–j).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 5i-j.

claim: Manipulating Plk4 protein levels does not reduce deuterosome or basal body number, nor does increasing the complement of parental centrioles.
source: In sum, manipulating Plk4 protein levels does not reduce deuterosome or basal body number, nor does increasing the complement of parental centrioles.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in Figure 5.

claim: Airway multiciliated cells grown in vitro display a broad range in centriole number, from 100 to 600 centrioles per cell.
source: We discovered that airway multiciliated cells grown in vitro display a broad range in centriole number, from 100 to 600 centrioles per cell (Figure 4).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4.

claim: Quantification of centriole number in vivo showed a similar variation in centriole abundance as observed in vitro.
source: Quantification of centriole number showed a similar variation in centriole abundance (Figure 6b).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 6b.

claim: There was a direct relationship between centriole number and surface area in vivo, as larger MCC contained more centrioles compared to smaller cells.
source: Consistent with the measurements in vitro, there was a direct relationship between centriole number and surface area, as larger MCC contained more centrioles compared to smaller cells (Figure 6b–d).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 6b-d.

claim: Culture and differentiation of basal cells on increasing concentrations of extracellular collagen resulted in a dose-dependent increase in cell surface area.
source: Culture and differentiation of basal cells on increasing concentrations of extracellular collagen resulted in a dose-dependent increase in cell surface area (Figure 7a–b).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 7a-b.

claim: Centriole abundance increased in a dose-dependent manner with increasing concentrations of extracellular collagen.
source: Remarkably, centriole abundance also increased in a dose-dependent manner (Figure 7c).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 7c.

claim: Although cells grown on higher collagen concentrations contained a larger surface area, they were shallower in depth, resulting in a similar overall cell volume.
source: Although the cells contained a larger surface area, they were shallower in depth, resulting in a similar overall cell volume (Figure 7a and d–e).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 7a and d-e.

claim: The size of surface area, but not overall cell volume, appears to dictate centriole abundance during amplification.
source: Thus, the size of surface area, but not overall cell volume, appears to dictate centriole abundance during amplification.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in Figure 7.

claim: Cells grown on higher concentrations of collagen formed a higher proportion of deuterosomes per cell on average.
source: Indeed, cells grown on higher concentrations of collagen formed a higher proportion of deuterosomes per cell on average (Figure 7f–g).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 7f-g.

claim: A cell-intrinsic surface area-dependent process establishes centriole abundance, potentially by modulating deuterosome number.
source: Collectively, these results indicate that a cell-intrinsic surface area-dependent process establishes centriole abundance, potentially by modulating deuterosome number.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in Figure 7.

claim: Although the PC are not critical for deuterosome biogenesis, they may help to control the number of deuterosomes formed, as well as the timing of their assembly and disassembly.
source: We interpret these data to suggest that, although the PC are not critical for deuterosome biogenesis, they may help to control the number of deuterosomes formed, as well as the timing of their assembly and disassembly.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: Loss of parental centrioles in dividing retinal pigment epithelial cells has been shown to trigger a p53-mediated stress response that inhibits their proliferation.
source: Loss of parental centrioles (and thus, centrosomes) in dividing retinal pigment epithelial cells has been shown to trigger a p53-mediated stress response that inhibits their proliferation (Fong et al., 2016; Lambrus et al., 2016; Meitinger et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Loss of the PC in airway basal cells did not block or slow their growth.
source: Yet, loss of the PC in airway basal cells did not block or slow their growth, suggesting that the downstream consequences may differ in various cells or tissues.
evidence: This is an observation from the experiments and an inference about cell-type specific responses.

claim: Mutations in components of the centriole assembly pathway are a major cause of microcephaly.
source: For example, mutations in components of the centriole assembly pathway are a major cause of microcephaly (Jayaraman et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Mutations in centrosome duplication factors can cause cystic and fibrotic kidney diseases.
source: In contrast, mutations in centrosome duplication factors can also cause cystic and fibrotic kidney diseases (Reiter and Leroux, 2017; Srivastava et al., 2017), which are characterized in part by enhanced and sustained cell proliferation.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The response of cells to centrosome loss, and the p53-dependent mitotic surveillance mechanism that senses this defect, may be cell- and tissue specific.
source: Therefore, the response of cells to centrosome loss, and the p53-dependent mitotic surveillance mechanism that senses this defect, may be cell- and tissue specific.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from comparing different cell types and disease phenotypes.

claim: Plk4 is absent in a number of organisms that contain centrioles, such as the unicellular ciliates Chlamydomonas and Tetrahymena.
source: However, Plk4 is absent in a number of organisms that contain centrioles. For example, the unicellular ciliates Chlamydomonas and Tetrahymena are able to assembly and duplicate their centrioles (basal bodies) without Plk4 (Carvalho-Santos et al., 2011; Dutcher and O'Toole, 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Plk4-interacting proteins such as STIL and Cep152 are missing in a number of organisms with centrioles.
source: Similarly, Plk4-interacting proteins such as STIL and Cep152 are missing in a number of organisms with centrioles (Carvalho-Santos et al., 2011), highlighting the presence of other mechanisms that allow for control of centriole formation.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Certain mammalian cell types may have adapted mechanisms to initiate centriologenesis independent of Plk4 kinase function.
source: Thus, even though components of the centriole assembly machinery are generally conserved throughout evolution, our results suggest that certain mammalian cell types may have adapted mechanisms to initiate centriologenesis independent of Plk4 kinase function.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results and evolutionary comparisons.

claim: Depletion of Plk4 in MTEC did cause a delay in centriologenesis, indicating that the protein itself might be needed for proper progression through the various stages of centriole assembly.
source: Depletion of Plk4 in MTEC did cause a delay in centriologenesis, indicating that the protein itself might be needed for proper progression through the various stages of centriole assembly.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: Differentiating, non-dividing MCC repurpose the mitotic regulatory circuitry involving CDK1/Plk1/APC-C to control the timely progression of centriole amplification, maturation, and motile ciliogenesis while avoiding reentry into mitosis.
source: For example, it was shown that differentiating, non-dividing MCC repurpose the mitotic regulatory circuitry involving CDK1/Plk1/APC-C to control the timely progression of centriole amplification, maturation, and motile ciliogenesis while avoiding reentry into mitosis (Al Jord et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: CDK2 was required in MCC to initiate the motile ciliogenesis program independent of cell cycle progression.
source: Another study found that CDK2, the kinase responsible for G1-S phase transition, was also required in MCC to initiate the motile ciliogenesis program independent of cell cycle progression (Vladar et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Plk4 functions as a homeostatic clock to ensure centrioles grow to the correct size in Drosophila.
source: Consistent with this theory, a recent study in Drosophila identified a role for Plk4 in regulating the rate and period of procentriole growth (Aydogan et al., 2018), demonstrating that Plk4 functions as a homeostatic clock to ensure centrioles grow to the correct size.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: MCC lacking Plk4 initiated centriole assembly to the same extent as control cells, were delayed in passage through the growth and maturation phases, but eventually 'caught up'.
source: Indeed, we found that MCC lacking Plk4 initiated centriole assembly to the same extent as control cells, were delayed in passage through the growth and maturation phases, but eventually 'caught up' (Figure 5).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Multiciliated cells lacking Plk4 contained the same number of centrioles on average when fully mature at ALI21.
source: Importantly, multiciliated cells lacking Plk4 contained the same number of centrioles on average when fully mature at ALI21, further indicating that it is not critical for regulating number per se.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 5.

claim: Overexpression of Plk4 in MTEC or in Xenopus larvae MCC did not result in increased centriole number.
source: Moreover, overexpression of Plk4 in MTEC (Figure 5) or in Xenopus larvae MCC (Klos Dehring et al., 2013) did not result in increased centriole number.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 5 and a citation to previous literature.

claim: Plk4 may play a similar role as CDK1/CDK2/Plk1/APC-C, by participating in a temporal regulatory mechanism that mediates passage through the various centriole assembly steps.
source: Thus, Plk4 may play a similar role as CDK1/CDK2/Plk1/APC-C, by participating in a temporal regulatory mechanism that mediates passage through the various centriole assembly steps.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the experimental findings and comparison to other kinases.

claim: The ciliogenesis program initiates roughly 2 days after basal cells have already established their size and surface area at ALI0 in the MTEC culture system.
source: One advantage of using the MTEC culture system is that the ciliogenesis program initiates roughly 2 days after basal cells have already established their size and surface area at ALI0.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental system.

claim: By growing cells on increasing extracellular collagen matrix density during the proliferation phase, cells formed more centrioles once fully differentiated, suggesting that the centriole amplification machinery responds to the change in surface area.
source: By growing cells on increasing extracellular collagen matrix density during the proliferation phase, we caused the enlargement of cell surface area before the transcriptional ciliogenesis program initiated. We discovered that cells formed more centrioles once fully differentiated, suggesting that the centriole amplification machinery responds to the change in surface area.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental manipulation described in Figure 7.

claim: Constitutive overexpression of Plk4 resulted in the formation of excess PC, but did not alter final centriole number or surface area.
source: Although constitutive overexpression of Plk4 did result in the formation of excess PC, it did not alter final centriole number or surface area (Figure 5 and data not shown).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 5.

claim: An apical actin network in MCC plays a critical role in modulating the surface area, regulating centriole migration and docking at the plasma membrane, ensuring the even distribution of centrioles across the cell surface, and orienting (planar polarization) of centrioles.
source: It is well established that an apical actin network in MCC plays a critical role in modulating the surface area, regulating centriole migration and docking at the plasma membrane, ensuring the even distribution of centrioles across the cell surface, and orienting (planar polarization) of centrioles (Antoniades et al., 2014; Herawati et al., 2016; Kulkarni et al., 2018; Mahuzier et al., 2018; Pan et al., 2007; Sedzinski et al., 2016; Sedzinski et al., 2017; Werner et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to previous literature.

claim: Variations in surface area may result in corresponding changes to the size of the apical actin lattice, which could then instruct the centriologenesis program to generate more centrioles.
